title: Multi-tenant leaky-bucket priority tiers and staged degradation playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background:
Redwood needs a predictable, low-latency degradation path when demand spikes or a region degrades. Current per-tenant token-buckets are coarse and do not express priority classes (billing tier / SLO tier / customer-critical). We also lack a compact set of graceful degradation modes that can be applied deterministically by admission control when shedding load.

Goal:
Design and implement a multi-tenant leaky-bucket admission controller that enforces priority tiers, enables prioritized KV-cache eviction hints, and triggers a staged degradation pipeline (full -> slim -> summary -> reject) with clear SLO mapping and observability. The system should work across regions and support fast failover: requests can be re-routed or degraded consistently during multi-region recovery.

Constraints & non-goals:
- Non-goal: replace quota billing; this is a runtime protection layer only.
- Must not require per-request heavyweight DB lookups; tenant metadata should be cached in the admission service.
- Keep tail-latency impact minimal: admission decision must complete in <1ms median.

Proposed design (summary):
1) Priority tiers: map tenants to 3 tiers (gold/silver/bronze) based on SLO commitments and usage class. Tier metadata includes min-throughput reservation, refill rate, and degrade-policy sequence.
2) Multi-tenant leaky-buckets: admission controller keeps an in-memory leaky-bucket per-tenant and a shared fast-path for small tenants (aggregated buckets). Buckets account for token cost estimated by request size and model selection.
3) Staged degradation pipeline: when tokens insufficient, admission returns a degradation instruction rather than a blunt rejection. Degradation modes (ordered):
   - response-slim: strip optional metadata, disable traces, reduce beam/return shorter max_tokens
   - cache-prefetch: prefer responses from KV cache or prefix cache, return best-effort cached output
   - summary-only: run condensed prompt path that yields short summary instead of full result
   - degrade-to-embedding: return embeddings with guidance to client to synthesize locally (for search use-cases)
   - reject-with-429: final fallback that returns rate-limit with suggested retry-after and optional operator message
4) KV cache hints: when admission plans to degrade, it emits eviction hints and prefetch priorities to the serving layer to surface best cached prefixes for silver/bronze tenants.
5) Multi-region failover behavior: buckets have a cross-region coordination tag. On region failover, admission controller shifts refill rates per-policy and can pre-degrade non-primary-region requests to ensure primary customers keep SLOs.
6) Observability: expose per-tenant token levels, degradation counts, and SLO burn rate to Console and add an alert when graceful-degrade rate exceeds threshold for 5m.

Risks/Trade-offs:
- Increased memory for per-tenant buckets; mitigated by aggregating low-volume tenants and TTL eviction.
- Decision complexity increases client behavior variability; ensure SDKs surface degradation hints to app logic.

Deliverables:
- Design doc (Confluence) with formal SLO mapping and API contract for degradation instructions.
- Admission controller implementation + unit/integration tests.
- Console dashboard + alerts.
- On-call runbook updates and customer-facing docs explaining degraded responses and suggested client handling.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller enforces per-tenant leaky-bucket policy and respects priority tiers in synthetic load tests
Staged degradation instructions are returned to the runtime and applied: response-slim, cache-prefetch, summary-only, degrade-to-embedding, reject-with-429
Admission decision latency median < 1ms in production-like load tests
Dashboard shows per-tenant token usage, degrade rate, and a burn-rate based alert configured
End-to-end test for multi-region failover: when primary region simulated down, controller transitions non-primary tenants according to policy and primary tenants maintain min-throughput reservation
implementation_steps: Write detailed design doc and SLO->tier mapping (Confluence: /confluence/rw/admission/leaky-bucket-design)
Prototype in canary: in-memory buckets + aggregated-bucket fallback; wire to a feature flag
Add degradation instruction proto and wire to runtime admission hook
Integrate KV-cache hint API: eviction and prefetch priority headers
Build Console dashboard and test alerts in staging
Run failover simulation test across two regions and iterate policies
Roll out in stages: canary (1%), limited tenant opt-in, 50% rollout, full rollout
metrics_and_dashboards: Console chart: admission.degrade.rate by tenant tier (gold/silver/bronze)
Alert: >5% degrade rate sustained for 5m for gold tier -> pager
SLO burn dashboard: request_latency_slo.burn_rate by tenant mapped to admission actions
KV cache hit ratio delta when cache-prefetch triggers
runbook_snippets: If degrade rate for gold tier > 5% and errors increase: toggle feature flag to force-reject-degraded for non-critical bundles, page reliability-oncall
During region failover: set refill-multiplier on primary tenants to 2.0 for 10m and enable cross-region-routing-exemption for gold tier
If admission decision latency spikes: roll back canary, inspect admission CPU/memory, check aggregated-bucket eviction counters
